label: original-phase token right after an "a"
explanation: Fires in the original (input) phase on the step right after the letter a was input, whatever the current token is (prev_tok=a gives 19.7x lift and 89% of activation mass). The largest activations (~1.0 of max) come at the step after a doubled "a a" pair, and the "a a" step itself is also strong (~0.6). A weaker tail (0.05-0.4 of max) fires two steps after an a, which accounts for most missed low-quartile activations. It is essentially silent when a appears at t>=7 (late positions), and does not fire at t=0, in the copy phase, or (beyond rare tiny values) on the delimiter. The current input token and L have little effect.

issues: Core claim holds. On test the predicate scores precision 0.960, recall 0.533, F1 0.685 and mass recall 0.881. prev_tok=a has 19.7x lift and 0.887 of the mass. Copy-phase activity is exactly 0. t=0 is 0. The delimiter step holds 0.6% of the mass, and (phase==1)&prev_tok==a has precision only 0.13. Rates by in_tok are flat (1.1-1.3x) and rates by L are flat (0.8-1.2x).

Off-by-one in the explanation. It says the feature goes quiet when the 'a' is at t>=7, but the predicate's cutoff (current t<=6) puts the 'a' at t<=5. With the 'a' at t=5 (current t=6), precision is 0.68 and mass is 2.1%. With the 'a' at t=6 (current t=7), precision drops to 0.15 and mass is 0.2%. So the feature goes quiet when the 'a' is at t>=6, not t>=7.

The tail is described wrongly. It is not mostly 'two steps after an a'. Steps two after an 'a' (prev2=a, prev!=a) account for about 24% of active count (8.7% of mass). A separate, unmentioned weak tail of about 0.01-0.1 fires in sequences with no 'a' seen yet: ~seen(a) covers 20.5% of active count but only 2.4% of mass, at precision 0.01, and sits mostly around t=4 (e.g. '2 q o w [f:0.06]'). The two tails are about the same size, so 'most of the low-quartile misses' overclaims.

Minor systematic weakening on a repeated, non-adjacent 'a'. prev_tok==a with an earlier 'a' and prev2!=a has precision 0.52 (n=4852, 1.4% of mass). Example false positive on test: 'a n x a *1*' is inactive after the second 'a'. Restricting to the first 'a' (n_seen([a])==1) gives precision 0.972 at nearly the same recall. The feature is really about the first 'a', apart from doubled 'a a'.

Magnitude claims check out roughly. Steps right after a doubled 'a a' have precision 0.956, and 5.1% of them fall in the top quartile versus 0.06% in the bottom quartile. The second 'a' of a pair is also high-quartile.
None of these gaps carries much mass. A better predicate that adds the two-step tail only for the first 'a' improves test F1 from 0.685 to 0.784, with precision 0.822 and mass recall 0.960.
skeptic.revised_label: original-phase step right after the first "a" (t <= 6), weaker two steps after
